-->

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug


**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR will cause the legacy AWS provider to select a health check port which utilises the appropriate protocol if an SSL health check is used. Prior to this the provider would simply pick the first port in the listener list, which could be a HTTP/TCP port, causing SSL health checks to fail.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

-->
Fixes #83070

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".
-->
```release-note
Users specifying "HTTPS" or "SSL" on the `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol` will need to ensure an SSL or HTTPS listener is available to for use on the health check. if no HTTPS or SSL listener is available, and error will be produced.
```

issue_context.title: [cloudprovider-aws] AWS legacy cloud provider Load Balancer health check can use non-SSL port with SSL health check
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When a load balancer is created via the AWS Cloud Provider can now use SSL, added in K8s v1.14 as part of this PR: #70309 which attempted to address this issue: #45746.

An unintended side effect of this change is that the health check port is not picked in a sensible manner - rather it will simply pick the first in the listener list. This can cause the SSL health check to utilise a non-SSL port, which subsequently will cause the health check to fail.

**What you expected to happen**:
The port used on the SSL health check should be picked sensibly based on the NodePort that supports HTTPS/SSL. (e.g. Has a certificate, or checks which listener is using the `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports` annotation)

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Create a cluster on running on AWS EC2 utilising the legacy cloud provider, then deploy an ingress service (we ran into this issue using traefik, and the traefik Helm chart found here: https://github.com/helm/charts/tree/master/stable/traefik). Provided the http port is first under the `ports:` declaration it should reproduce the issue.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.14.6
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: AWS EC2
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CoreOS
- Install tools: Tectonic Installer

review_comments: `listener.Protocol` is the frontend protocol.  So are you using the frontend protocol in case the listener is HTTPS/SSL on the frontend and insecure on the backend?

Now that you point this out, it does kind of feel like `listener.InstanceProtocol` should be getting used here, but the docs on the type are a bit confusing (they say this field must be the same as the frontend protocol, but it's obviously supposed to be the backend protocol) so I'm not sure: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/elb/#Listener

this indeed should be listeners.InstanceProtocol. 
Also, this will break when `ServiceAnnotationLoadBalancerBEProtocol` is set to HTTPS, but no certificated is used. 
I'm not sure whether there are ppl have such configuration combination but it's valid if ppl wants TCP termination and SSL healthcheck on backend(disclaimer: i didn't test whether this is valid on CLB)
Will this break current behavior?  Should we fall back to picking the first port here too instead of erroring?

I'm thinking its actually ok, because we're making the assumption that the backend protocol annotation dictates the health check protocol, and AFAIK the only time a user should choose a secure backend protocol is if all their instance ports are secure.  (According to the [k8s aws service loadbalancer docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#ssl-support-on-aws), when using mixed ports the user should select the insecure protocol for backend protocol).  @justinsb @M00nF1sh can you confirm that its ok to fail when backend protocol annotation is secure and there are no ports with a *secure frontend protocol*?

In this case, when the annotation (Backend) protocol is not HTTPS or SSL (meaning it is HTTP or TCP) , we pick the first listener that has an instance port.  Should we instead be picking the first listener that does not have HTTPS or SSL as its protocol?
This depends - is it safe to assume that if the backend protocol is not HTTPS/SSL then there should be no HTTPS/SSL endpoints on the loadbalancer?

No that's not a safe assumption, there can be frontend SSL listeners with TCP backend listeners if you want SSL termination at the load balancer.  But I think what you have makes sense, if we have decided the health check protocol is TCP, then it will work on any open port.
